ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Commercial Act (Act No. 1000, as amended), Articles 19, 21, 23, 24, 26, 289 and 292; Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Information (Act No. 8635, as amended), Articles 2, 5, 5-2 and 7; Financial Transaction Reports Act (Act No. 5393, as amended), Articles 3, 4 and 5-2; Enforcement Decree of the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Information (Presidential Decree No. 19800, as amended), Article 10; Foreign Investment Promotion Act (Act No. 5559, as amended), Article 5 and its Enforcement Decree; Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) Customer Due Diligence Guidelines.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or equivalent official entity in the foreign shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path for Apostille Convention states: local notarization where required then Apostille certificate issued by the competent Apostille authority of the issuing country then licensed Korean translation then submission to Korean registry and bank. Consular legalization is not added; for non-Apostille states, use Korean Embassy Consular Legalization exclusively. Apostille and Consular legalization are parallel and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing for the Foreign Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company registry or government authority with custody of the corporate register in the foreign shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path for Apostille Convention states: notarize issuer signature if required, obtain Apostille from the competent authority, produce certified Korean translation, submit to Korean filing officer. For non-Apostille states, obtain Consular Legalization from the Korean Embassy or Consulate before translation. Never chain Apostille after Consular Legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney for Incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the foreign shareholder, signed by directors and notarized by a local notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: notarize directors' signatures, issue Apostille from competent authority, translate into Korean, submit. For non-Apostille states: notarize locally, then Consular Legalization at the Korean diplomatic mission. The two routes are exclusive alternatives; no sequential combination is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Copy of Articles of Association or Memorandum of Association of the Foreign Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign shareholder's company secretary or company registry certified extraction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: certify extract, notarize certifying officer's signature if demanded, attach Apostille, translate into Korean, file. For non-Apostille states, use Consular Legalization of the Korean Consulate instead of Apostille. The paths are mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original Bank Reference Letter for the Foreign Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate relationship bank of the foreign shareholder, sealed and dated
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: bank officer's signature and bank seal notarized locally, Apostille attached, certified Korean translation submitted to the target Korean bank. For non-Apostille states: notarize bank seal, then obtain Consular Legalization from the Korean Consulate. If Apostille is used, Consular Legalization must not be added.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before any Korean registry filing, the foreign shareholder, its directors, officers, ultimate beneficial owners at or above 25%, and all signatories must be screened against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, US OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HM Treasury sanctions list, and the Korean FIU list of designated persons and suspected-financing notifications. PEP screening includes current and former foreign and domestic PEPs for twelve months after leaving office, together with family members and close associates. Any hit, low-credit-risk but irregular source-of-funds profile, or link to a jurisdiction on the FATF grey list triggers enhanced due diligence including verified identification documents, source-of-wealth explanation, and a written engagement risk rating. Results are documented in the AML file and refreshed before every material transaction.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registry (i-Register) and National Tax Service Hometax portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A Yuhan Hoesa's statutory name must be written in Hangeul and may additionally carry a Latin or foreign-script transliteration. The registry applies a four-tier naming test: exact string identity, phonetic and visually similar transliteration collision, identical or substantially identical principal business under ISIC 6201 and mobile utility application scope, and territorial exclusivity within the Seoul Central District Court registration district. The suffix Yuhan Hoesa must appear. Foreign trade names are transliterated into Hangeul, and an English trade name may be registered only if the Hangeul transliteration is reflected in the registry record.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant or local counsel must file a written objection with the Commercial Registration Officer of the Seoul Central District Court within 14 days of receiving notice, specifying the requested name, the registry entry relied upon for distinction, and legal arguments under the Commercial Act trade-name articles. The registrar shall answer in writing; if the rejection is confirmed, counsel may file an administrative appeal with the Administrative Appeals Division of the Ministry of Court Administration within 60 days, and thereafter an administrative lawsuit in the Seoul Administrative Court within 90 days. Simultaneously, a new reservation may be filed after amending the name with a differentiating suffix or transliteration.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Korean law does not impose a per se ban on virtual offices or commercial mailboxes for software developers, but registration of a Yuhan Hoesa with a virtual address is operationally risky. The district National Tax Service and financial institutions require the actual place of business and may reject home-office or post-office-box addresses unless supported by a written lease, physical reception service, and evidence that management, books, and data are accessible from that address. For a freemium mobile utility app with Apple and Google as app-store distributors, banks will usually demand an operating lease or co-working contract; a mere mailbox without substance is unlikely to satisfy customer due diligence for corporate account opening and VAT registration. A virtual office is therefore legally permissible in form but substantially disfavored; a leased serviced office is recommended for commercial substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: low-to-moderate. Unannounced physical inspection by the municipal tax office or commercial registry occurs in approximately 10-15% of cases where a registered virtual office is used within the first two years; probability rises to 30-35% if VAT invoices are irregular, tenant directory mismatches appear, or suspicious transaction reports have been filed. Checklist: verify registered address matches lease, utilities, employee registrations and tax office records; post a nameplate and keep a responsible manager available during business hours; maintain signed contracts, server and analytics logs, and accounting records at the seat; keep board-authorized corporate documentation in Korea; register employees for social insurance at the same address; and train personnel to provide a site-access protocol to tax officials.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of South Korea (상법), Articles 288-289 (incorporation), Article 290 (articles of incorporation), Article 292 (registration), Article 317 (registration of incorporation), and Article 543 (limited liability company provisions).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Supreme Court Registry Office (법원등기국) via the local district court registry (지방법원 등기과) with jurisdiction over the registered office address.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation (법인설립등기신청서) and Articles of Incorporation (정관) duly notarized.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. South Korea does not impose a minimum paid-up capital for a Yuhan Hoesa (LLC). However, the capital must be fully paid-in at incorporation and deposited into a temporary escrow account with a Korean bank, which is released upon issuance of the certificate of incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] (YUHAN HOESA) ADOPTED BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT IN LIEU OF A MEETING ON [DATE] AT [TIME] AT THE REGISTERED OFFICE OF THE COMPANY. WHEREAS, the Company was incorporated under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea on [DATE] with registration number [REGISTRATION NO.]; WHEREAS, the Board of Directors is authorized to take all actions necessary to commence business operations and to establish corporate governance; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS: 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: The initial share capital of KRW [AMOUNT] has been fully subscribed and paid in by the shareholders as per the Articles of Incorporation. The Board acknowledges receipt of the capital contribution and directs the Chief Financial Officer to record the same in the corporate books. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The Board hereby authorizes the opening of corporate bank accounts with [BANK NAME] and designates the following signatories: [NAME], [POSITION], and [NAME], [POSITION], each with individual authority to transact, sign checks, and execute banking documents. The bank is instructed to honor any two signatures for amounts exceeding KRW [THRESHOLD]. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: The registered office of the Company shall be at [ADDRESS], as stated in the Articles of Incorporation. The Board ratifies the lease agreement and authorizes the payment of rent and utilities. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: The Board appoints [NAME] as Chief Executive Officer (대표이사), [NAME] as Chief Financial Officer (재무이사), and [NAME] as Auditor (감사) for a term of [TERM] years. Each officer shall have the powers and duties as prescribed by law and the Articles of Incorporation. 5. CORPORATE SEAL AND DOCUMENTATION: The Board approves the creation and use of a corporate seal (법인인감) and authorizes the CEO to register the seal with the registry office. 6. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION: The Board authorizes any officer to execute all documents, file all registrations, and take all actions necessary to effectuate the foregoing resolutions. This resolution is effective immediately and shall be filed with the corporate records. ADOPTED this [DAY] day of [MONTH], [YEAR].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve Company Name and Prepare Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court Registry Office (online via IROS system) and a local notary public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application through the IROS (Internet Registration Office System) to ensure the proposed company name is not identical to existing registered entities. Simultaneously, draft the Articles of Incorporation (정관) in Korean, including the company name, purpose (mobile utility software development and distribution), registered office address, capital amount, and number of shares. The articles must be notarized by a notary public. Ensure all shareholders' signatures are notarized. The name reservation is valid for 6 months.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of all shareholders and directors
Power of attorney if using an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to similarity, select an alternative name and resubmit. If the notary requires corrections, amend the articles and re-notarize.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit Paid-in Capital into Escrow Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank in South Korea (e.g., Kookmin, Shinhan, Woori)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary escrow account in the name of the company being formed with a Korean bank. Each shareholder must transfer their respective capital contribution to this account. The bank will issue a certificate of deposit (예치증명서) confirming the total paid-in capital. This certificate is required for the incorporation registration. The funds are frozen until the company is registered, after which they are released to the company's operational account.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the source of funds, provide additional documentation such as bank statements or gift declarations. If the deposit is incomplete, arrange for full payment before proceeding.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation Application with Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Court Registry Office (지방법원 등기과) having jurisdiction over the registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the incorporation registration application (법인설립등기신청서) to the court registry office. Attach the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the certificate of capital deposit, the list of directors and auditor, and the written consent of each director to accept their appointment. The application must be filed within 2 weeks of the notarization of the articles. The court will review the documents and, if satisfactory, issue a Certificate of Incorporation (법인등기부등본).
required_dossiers: Certificate of capital deposit from bank
List of directors and auditor with consent forms
Power of attorney if filed by agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a correction order, rectify the deficiencies within the given period (usually 2 weeks). If the application is rejected, appeal or resubmit after correcting the issues. Legal counsel may be engaged to expedite.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Business Tax and Obtain Corporate Seal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via Hometax online portal and local district tax office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Certificate of Incorporation, register for business tax (사업자등록) with the NTS within 20 days. Provide the certificate of incorporation, articles, and identification. The NTS will issue a business registration certificate (사업자등록증). Simultaneously, register the corporate seal (법인인감) with the court registry office to obtain a seal certificate (인감증명서). This is required for banking and legal transactions.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NTS queries the business purpose, provide a detailed description of the mobile utility app development and distribution. If the seal registration is delayed, request expedited processing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - The entity is a pure digital software developer with no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operations. No fire safety certification, structural load inspections, or workplace safety approvals are required beyond standard office occupancy permits.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, operating the electronic Home Tax Service (HTS) portal at hometax.go.kr; indirect tax registration and e-tax invoice reporting are lodged through that portal, while export customs clearance and export declaration are administered by Korea Customs Service (KCS).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident foreign company that supplies goods or services in Korea, or receives Korean-source income, must obtain a Korean Business Registration Number (the statutory TIN for corporate tax and VAT). Before applying, the foreign company appoints a domestic tax representative if it has no Korean place of business. The representative submits to the National Tax Service through Home Tax Service: (i) Certificate of Incorporation and Articles of Association, (ii) foreign business license or certificate of registration translated into English or Korean, (iii) power of attorney appointing the tax representative, and (iv) a statement of the expected Korean business scope and commencement date. The NTS issues the 10-digit business registration number, which is simultaneously used for corporate tax, VAT, and employee withholding; the registration is effective retroactively to the business commencement date. Digital-service-only businesses selling to Korean consumers are treated as registered taxable persons for VAT and must file VAT returns using the same registration number, with no requirement for paid-in capital.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. South Korea does not allow a check-the-box or fiscal transparency election for a Yuhan Hoesa; a resident limited company is always a separate taxable entity subject to entity-level corporate income tax. No hybrid mismatch entity election is available, although transfer pricing and treaty residence declarations must be filed with the NTS via the International Tax Adjustment Act.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no statutory turnover threshold that exempts a foreign or domestic supplier from VAT registration; any person carrying on a business making taxable supplies in South Korea must register. A Simplified Taxpayer filing regime is available only for individual proprietors with annual VAT-exclusive revenue below KRW 80,000,000, but such taxpayers remain registered and must file semi-annual simplified VAT returns.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Korea enforces an electronic tax invoice mandate through the NTS HomeTax e-invoice system. B2B suppliers with transactions subject to VAT must issue electronic tax invoices, transmit them to NTS by no later than the day following the supply, and use an NTS-issued invoice identification number. APIs and machine-to-machine ERP integration are available through approved e-invoice service providers and the HomeTax open interface; each submitted e-invoice receives immediate validation of buyer and seller registration numbers and format, although Korea generally validates rather than pre-clears in real time. Anti-fraud control includes automatic comparison of issued, transmitted, and received e-tax invoices, refusal management, cash receipt issuance obligations for consumer sales, and automatic audit flags for missing, delayed, or false digital stamps. The fiscal digital evidence is the NTS e-Tax Invoice acceptance record, not a physical stamp.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Korean VAT Act, goods and services exported from Korea are zero-rated at 0% when there is a real export of goods evidenced by Korea Customs Service clearance, or a supply of services to non-residents for use outside Korea. For the mobile utility software app, zero-rating is available when the app is distributed through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing to non-Korean account holders, the download or use of the app occurs outside Korea, and the proceeds are collected in foreign currency and repatriated. The supplier must obtain the app store settlement report, transaction-level logs with country codes, and, for B2B export invoices, the foreign purchaser business registration evidence. Zero-rating is not automatic: the VAT return must separately disclose zero-rated supplies and attach export settlement documentation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service electronic Export Declaration, which is the Korean equivalent of a shipping bill or bill of entry and evidences that the goods left Korea
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill, or for digital service exports the app store settlement report plus carrier transit receipt where a physical export exists
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or a Korean bank Foreign Exchange Earnings Certificate showing actual collection of export proceeds in hard currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS compares export zero-rating claims with Korea Customs Service clearance records, foreign exchange bank receipts, and digital platform settlement files. If the claimed export is false, overstated, or not supported by documentation, the zero rate is reversed, the unpaid 10% VAT is assessed with statutory negligence under the VAT Act, additional tax of up to 40% can be imposed for intentional evasion or fraudulent invoices, and interest under the Framework Act on National Taxes accrues from the original filing date. Criminal referral under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act is possible for deliberate fabrication of export documentation or circular foreign exchange arrangements. Claimed refunds discovered to be improper are clawed back with the same statutory additions before any refund setoff.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) as the central monetary authority, with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a liberalized current-account convertibility regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its Enforcement Decree. The Korean won (KRW) is fully convertible for legitimate trade, service, dividend remittance, and salary transactions; current-account payments are generally processed without prior approval through authorized foreign exchange banks. Capital-account convertibility, however, is subject to notification or approval requirements for inward direct investment, outward investment, loans, and financial derivatives. Export proceeds must be collected into a resident foreign currency deposit account at a domestic foreign exchange bank within the statutory collection period, but there is no mandatory conversion ratio into KRW. Profit remittance, including dividends for foreign shareholders, is technically free for non-residents provided the company is classified as a foreign-invested enterprise and submits withholding tax certificates; however, practical hurdles include historical tax clearance confirmations, annual external audit reports, and the need to prove the source of funds through FEIS filing. The Bank of Korea and selected foreign exchange banks monitor large and unusual cross-border flows under the Foreign Exchange Information System; any non-compliance can result in administrative fines and delays. Overall, the KRW is assessed as freely usable on current account and substantially convertible on a notified, transaction-based capital account.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, Korean exporters must collect proceeds from export declarations within one year from the date of exportation, extendable only with MOEF/BOK approval, and must deposit those proceeds into a foreign exchange bank resident foreign currency account. There is no statutorily mandated surrender conversion percentage; exporters may retain 100% of export proceeds in foreign currency, convert to KRW at the prevailing market rate, or apply the funds to eligible foreign currency payment obligations, all subject to bank-level FEIS reporting thresholds and anti-money laundering documentation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Very Low. South Korea imposes strict licensing under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act for electronic money, prepaid instruments, and payment services. Offshore digital EMI platforms that do not hold a Korean electronic financial business authorization cannot legally issue KRW accounts, FX settlement accounts, or provide cross-border treasury services to Korean domestic entities. A Yuhan Hoesa must use a locally licensed foreign exchange bank for operating cash and FX clearing; a non-bank EMI may be used only for ancillary outbound payouts if it is a registered overseas payment provider with a clear Korean contractual interface, but it cannot replace the primary clearing bank. The recommended route is a domestic foreign exchange bank with FEIS reporting capabilities.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: South Korea's financial institutions must verify identity under the Financial Transactions Information Act and the Real-Name Financial Transaction Guarantee Act. For a domestic Yuhan Hoesa, the statutory representative must generally appear in person at the domestic branch with the corporate seal registration certificate, business registration certificate, and personal identification. Remote video authentication is accepted for domestic individuals, but for corporates with non-resident shareholders, banks require at least one officer or director with a valid Korean ARC or a passport plus qualifying visa to attend the banking interview physically. Consular proxy opening is not generally recognized for corporate deposit accounts; a foreign shareholder may provide a notarized power of attorney to a Korean co-director, but the named statutory director and the designated account signatory must satisfy the bank's in-person KYC protocol before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistency between the declared business scope of mobile utility software and the expected transaction profile of highly active app-store fund flows triggers enhanced bank committee review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apple App Store and Google Play Console developer agreements, in-app purchase term sheets, third-party audited revenue projections, user growth dashboard exports, enterprise KYC forms, product technology documentation, and a written cash-flow topology explaining platform settlement cycles.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial ownership above the 25% threshold triggers enhanced due diligence for foreign UBOs under Korean AML regulations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Korean corporate registry extract, shareholder ledger, unencumbered share certificates, passports of foreign shareholders, proof of overseas address, source-of-wealth documentation such as bank statements and home-country tax returns, OECD CRS self-certification forms, and signed UBO declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The initial capital contribution appears as a lump-sum equity injection in KRW or USD and may be flagged as a suspicious deposit under Korean financial transaction analytics.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized capital contribution resolution, two-year bank statements of the originating account, signed director declaration of source of funds, validated business plan, inward investment reporting confirmation from the foreign exchange bank, and corporate tax filings reflecting subscribed capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments for IP licensing, royalty, or app-related technology services to an overseas parent or developer are flagged for potential base erosion and profit shifting.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed intellectual property license agreements, GitHub or software repository ownership evidence, transfer pricing documentation aligned with Korean informed compliance rules, local withholding tax and VAT schedules, explainable intragroup transaction mapping, and patent or trademark registration certificates.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity injections must follow the Foreign Investment Promotion Act when the Yuhan Hoesa is foreign-invested. Step one: file an investment notification with MOEF/KOTRA through the designated foreign exchange bank. Step two: open a foreign investor's foreign currency deposit account at that bank. Step three: remit the capital from the overseas investor's account via SWIFT, entering the appropriate Korean foreign exchange purpose code for inward direct investment and equity purchase. Step four: the bank registers the remittance in the Foreign Exchange Information System and issues a certificate of capital verification. Step five: funds may be converted into KRW at market rate and settled into the company's operational account. Non-investment current-account fund infusions must also be reported to the bank when thresholds are met, and all settlement documentation must be retained for five years.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Digital platform distributions from Apple and Google arrive through SWIFT MT103s into the Korean entity's foreign currency settlement account after the platform deduction cycle. For contractual or high-value disbursements, the company may use SWIFT MT103 direct transfers for services and royalties, commercial irrevocable letters of credit for hardware, content procurement or co-development agreements, and documentary collections for invoice-based settlements. All outbound payments must be encoded with the appropriate foreign exchange settlement purpose and a clear beneficiary invoice, and must be cleared through the bank's e-trade and FEIS portal to avoid reporting delays. The company should also maintain separate KRW operational and foreign currency settlement accounts to keep app-store proceeds reconcilable.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/KRW foreign exchange forward contracts for actual current-account trade or service exposure
FX swaps and cross-currency swaps used only for short-term liquidity management with an underlying real receivable or payable
Currency options, including vanilla puts and calls, permitted solely for hedge tenor and amount matching the app store settlement forecast
Rolling spot forwards for USD/KRW revenue in multi-month contractual cycles up to 110% of verified expected exposure

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible for resident Korean entities; any offshore NDF quoting would require explicit KR regulatory approval and is generally prohibited for domestic treasury use

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary General Meeting of Members and Approval of Annual Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate governance; no state filing is required, but approved financial statements must be presented to the members and annexed to the corporate income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after each fiscal year-end; for a December calendar year-end the meeting must be held by March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct tax fine, but directors and managers may incur personal liability for losses caused by missing the deadline; absence of approved annual financial statements prevents lawful profit distributions and permits the National Tax Service to reassess income on an estimated basis.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return and Financial Statement Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea; filed through the HomeTax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 of the year following the close of a December fiscal year, or within 3 months after the end of a non-December fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing triggers an additional tax equal to 20% of the calculated corporate income tax; underreporting triggers 10% of the omitted tax; intentional concealment triggers 40% of the omitted tax. Unpaid tax accrues a statutory daily late-payment surcharge of 0.025% per day, and persistent non-payment can lead to estimated assessment, asset seizure, business-place closure, and court-ordered dissolution or strike-off of an inactive company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax Return and Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent local government of the Si/Gun/Gu where the registered head office is located; filed through HomeTax or the local government electronic tax system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before April 30 of the following year for a December fiscal year; within 4 months after the end of a non-December fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A local filing penalty of 20% for non-reporting, 10% for underreporting, and a daily local tax arrears surcharge of 0.025% are imposed; enforcement may include seizure of bank accounts, revocation of the business registration, and administrative closure of the operating place.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax Preliminary Return and Payment for the January to June Period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service through the HomeTax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before July 25 of the same calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or underreporting triggers VAT additional taxes, including 10% of unpaid or underpaid VAT for underreporting, plus a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.025%; continued non-compliance permits estimated assessment, seizure of bank and App Store settlement proceeds, and administrative closure of the business.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax Final Return and Payment for the Preceding Calendar Year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service through the HomeTax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before January 25 of the following year for the preceding January to December taxable period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or underreporting triggers a VAT additional tax of 10% of the unpaid tax and a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.025%; persistent non-filing may result in estimated assessment, criminal complaint, asset seizure, and administrative strike-off of the inactive entity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory External Audit Report Filing with the Financial Supervisory Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service of Korea under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and Other Enterprises; internal delivery to members as part of the ordinary general meeting package
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the fiscal year-end, by April 30 for a calendar year; in any event before the date of the ordinary general meeting of members
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A company that is mandatorily subject to audit but fails to appoint an auditor or file the audit report is exposed to administrative penalties and criminal fines under the External Audit Act; the unaudited financial statements cannot validly support distributions, and the National Tax Service may treat the corporate income tax return as unfiled or unreliable.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Registry Amendment Filings for Director, Registered Office, Capital, and Member Changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the Local District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office; filed electronically through the Korean court registration system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 14 days after any event requiring registration; annual secretarial review must verify that all registrable changes have been reflected by March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Untimely registration is subject to a court-imposed non-registration fine of up to KRW 5,000,000, which is approximately USD 3,800; unregistered changes are ineffective against bona fide third parties, and repeated failure to maintain accurate registry records contributes to administrative strike-off after the company becomes non-operational.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Register Audit and Corporate Secretarial Compliance Certificate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate secretary and external legal counsel; the certificate is presented to the ordinary general meeting of members and retained in the corporate records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually before the ordinary general meeting and no later than March 31 following each calendar year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Deficient registers may invalidate the exercise of membership and management rights; directors and managers may be fined under the Commercial Act; inaccurate membership, pledge, and beneficial ownership records also expose the company to bank, payment provider, and AML compliance failures.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and Other Enterprises as amended, a Yuhan Hoesa must appoint an independent external auditor if its total assets at the end of the fiscal year exceed KRW 12 billion, approximately USD 9.2 million at prevailing exchange rates. This is a balance-sheet trigger; there are no separate turnover or headcount thresholds for a private Korean LLC. A mandatory audit also arises if the company is required by its articles of association, by a lender or regulatory condition, or by the Financial Supervisory Service to file an audit report. For a mobile utility app developer with ordinary App Store revenues, the KRW 12 billion total-asset threshold is the operative statutory benchmark.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS, the Korean adaptation of IFRS, is mandatory for listed companies and certain designated financial institutions. A non-listed Yuhan Hoesa may prepare financial statements under K-GAAP, the general corporate accounting standards for Korean businesses, or under the Accounting Standards for Small and Medium Enterprises if eligible. When the KRW 12 billion audit threshold is crossed, the financial statements and the independent auditor's report must be prepared in accordance with K-IFRS or the applicable K-GAAP framework recognized under Korean accounting standards. The corporate income tax return begins from financial accounting net income and applies the adjustments required by the Corporate Tax Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not maintain a public beneficial ownership register for private limited companies and does not impose an annual UBO confirmation filing on a Yuhan Hoesa. The company must, however, keep its Register of Members continuously current and must record every transfer of a membership interest; a transfer is effective against the company only after it is recorded or notified in the register. Director changes and registered office changes must be filed with the Commercial Registry within 14 days. The 30-day public reporting window for shareholding transfers applies under Korean capital markets law only to major shareholders of listed public corporations and is not applicable to this private LLC. AML-compliance practice requires the company to reconfirm beneficial ownership information at bank account openings, material financing events, and payment-provider due-diligence reviews.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Pledges and Charges on Membership Interests
Minute Book of Members' General Meetings and Director Resolutions
Corporate Seal Control and Document Execution Log

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 - 2,000 per year for registered office supervision, corporate secretarial administration, and agent services in Seoul
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 - 9,500 per year for a certified independent audit if the KRW 12 billion asset threshold is exceeded; if no statutory audit is required, USD 1,200 - 2,800 per year for a professional annual review and compilation package

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national corporate income tax (top bracket) + 2.4% local income surtax, aggregate 26.4% highest marginal rate
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SME rate: 9% on first KRW 200 million taxable income; R&D tax credit up to 30% of qualifying R&D expenditure; five-year corporate tax holiday for eligible foreign-invested enterprises in Free Economic Zones; IP Box regime providing 50% reduction (or full, for small business) on income from qualifying patented technology.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Return Form (NTS Form 44-1) filed electronically via NTS HomeTax (www.hometax.go.kr)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the fiscal year end (e.g., March 31 for calendar year-end taxpayers); an extension of up to 6 months may be granted for foreign-invested companies with approval.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Entity/Metadata Identification - business registration number, corporate name, head office address, representative director name, and fiscal year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare the Korea Taxpayer Identification Number (K-TIN) of the non-resident shareholder, and attach the certificate of alterable shareholder listing if non-resident ownership exceeds a threshold.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial Statement Income - net income per Korean GAAP adjusted to tax accounting basis
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile any permanent/temporary differences arising from cross-border transactions, including branch profits and foreign exchange differences.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax Adjustments and Sundry Dissolution - additions (non-deductible expenses, taxability of certain incomes) and subtractions (e.g., exempt dividends)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter treaty-based exemption or credit claims for foreign taxes paid; attach form for foreign tax credit under Article 57 of the Corporate Income Tax Act.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss Carryforward and Deduction Items - prior-year unexpired losses within 10 years, special deductions for overseas investment and IP royalties
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify that loss carryforward is limited to the local entity; no group relief consolidation with foreign parents.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable Base and Rate Application - compute taxable income and apply progressive rates: 9% up to KRW 200M; 19% KRW 200M–20B; 21% KRW 20B–300B; 24% over KRW 300B
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure transfer pricing adjustments have been reflected prior to computing taxable base; state the arm's length price.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax Computations and Payments - final corporate tax liability, deduct advance payments and credits, determine balance payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a payment to a non-resident shareholder is made, the withholding agent (the Korean company) must separately report the dividend WHT in the withholding tax return. State any reduced treaty rate claimed and attach the TRC.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 20% of tax due (40% if fraudulent); understatement: 10% (40% fraudulent); late payment: 0.022% per day of the unpaid tax; failure to submit documentation: up to KRW 10 million; criminal prosecution for willful evasion under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% national dividend withholding tax + 2% local income surtax)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply the treaty rate, the non-resident beneficial owner must, before the dividend payment date, submit to the Korean withholding agent: (i) an original Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued within the past year by its domestic tax authority; (ii) a certificate of beneficial ownership (Form No. 50) stating that the recipient is the ultimate beneficial owner and does not pass the dividend to any third party; and (iii) the treaty relief application filed via HomeTax. Where the full statutory WHT has been withheld, the non-resident may claim a refund within three years by filing a claim with the district NTS office. Non-compliance results in application of the full 22% WHT.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate for royalties and interest: 22% (same structure as dividends). Under Korea's bilateral tax treaties, royalty withholding is typically reduced to 10%–15% (e.g., 10% with Germany, 15% with some others), and interest is usually reduced to 10–12%. The same procedural TRC/Beneficial Ownership requirements apply.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: required when cross-border connected transactions exceed KRW 50 billion (KRW 50,000,000,000) per fiscal year; Master File and CbC Report: required when the multinational group's consolidated revenue exceeds KRW 1 trillion and the Korean entity's cross-border connected transactions exceed KRW 10 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea applies economic substance via the GAAR (Article 17, Framework Act on National Taxation) and established case law. For tax incentives (e.g., Free Economic Zones), the company must maintain actual business premises, hire residents, and perform core income-generating activities (CIGA) in Korea. A letterbox company will be denied treaty benefits and preferential tax rates.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Planning and submitting a corporate income tax return deliberately omitting revenue from in-app sales, fabricating expenses, or utilizing undisclosed foreign bank accounts to hide taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violation of Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act; penalty of imprisonment up to 5 years and/or fine up to twice (or three times for aggravated cases) the amount of evaded tax; plus additional 20% (or 40% if fraudulent) surcharge on the tax due.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly engage in, instruct, or conspire to commit tax evasion are personally liable for the unpaid tax and penalties; may be subject to criminal imprisonment, asset seizure, and a travel ban (blacklisting) pending investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Entering into offshore intercompany transactions (e.g., licensing of the mobile app IP to a related party in a tax haven) at non-arm's length prices, thereby shifting profits out of Korea without proper TP documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment under Article 4 and 5 of the International Tax Adjustment Act; additional tax assessment plus an understatement penalty of 10% (40% intentional) and late-payment interest; failure to produce prescribed documentation attracts a KRW 5 million per document penalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved transfer prices without an economic basis may be jointly liable for the adjusted tax if they acted negligently; criminal liability may arise under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act if the transfer pricing arrangement constitutes willful tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Sham Entity for Treaty Shopping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Korean LLC as a letterbox entity (no premises, employees, or business activities) to funnel royalty income out under a bilateral tax treaty, or to claim FEZ tax incentives without actual operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The NTS may deny treaty benefits under the Limitation on Benefits (LOB) clause and under the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (Article 17 of Framework Act on National Taxation); corporate tax is re-assessed at full statutory rates with a 40% penalty for abusive avoidance; the entity's approval may be revoked.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal liability for the corporate obligations if the court pierces the corporate veil for fraudulent or dishonest use of the entity; travel bans can be imposed, and criminal charges for tax avoidance may result in up to 5 years of imprisonment.
